blind_spot: The hook's block decision was checked against one output file being non-empty, never against the set of stacked sub-agent waiters or whether each was still live.

The V1.2/V1.7 rows compared the refusal text to 'Read-only file system' only. Mount isolation changed what the session can see, so the same correct refusal now reads 'No such file'. No check compared the row's expected text with the mount view.
The drill push triggers were never compared to vm_check.py's imports, and the V1 visibility rows never checked whether a session sees other repos' mounts. No check read either relationship.
The defect is a runtime decision: dev() spawning a second stack when a live one exists. No check:* compares whether account dev reuses a live stack.

The drill decided blocked from nc's printed text and docker's exit code, and never compared B's refused connect with what A's listener actually received. The relationship it broke, the attempt against the listener's own log, was never read.
Render-lock overlap is concurrency between lock and recording stage. Existing check:* gates read contents and wiring, never two stages holding the lock at once.
Unit tests and check gates see how the CLI builds the remote command, not whether a backgrounded job holds the ssh channel open. Only a live vm:check observes that.
No check compares a schema's hard length limits with the model's output-retry budget. The defect only appears in a live judge call, and no test runs one against the schema's limits.

98ed3bd: the fixture read origin/main from the ambient checkout and removed its control file outside finally, so it passed only where the ref existed. 37ecbdd: no check compares /tmp entries or lock-file cleanup, so a harness that leaks passes every gate.
i18n.sh passed with the key missing from every catalog, so no check tests whether an i18n.T() key is a member of pkg/i18n/locales. That membership relation was never compared.

The review-found converge fix covers a throw mid-setup, which the existing success-path tests never exercise. The drill fork defect only reproduces in a live vm:check run, which npm run ci does not execute.

Every check compares the renet security_opt validator against its own accepted-set fixture, never against Docker's accepted spellings. The broken relationship is validator versus Docker's name:value form, and no check observes Docker's behaviour.

Converge decides restarts from the live daemon container list and the mount's Rediaccfile. No check:* key compares that decision against a running daemon, so the static gates see only source and fixtures.

The 227 existing tests and the i18n and contract checks only compare successful responses and key parity. None checks what a request does when response headers never arrive, or what error text a refused connection produces, so a regression to an unbounded wait or a bare 'fetch failed' stays green.
Every check compares build output, types, i18n keys or contract shape. None runs a fetch against a stalled server, so no check observes the request deadline or the dropped error cause.
No check in the list reads the proxy client's request timeout or the error it raises when a request fails, so a stalled header phase is invisible to every gate.
